assertions.note: Six named files (evidence_pack.py, test_evidence_pack.py, README.md, LICENSE, example-evidence.json, review-cases.json) each carry inline content plus a content_sha256, not digests alone.

package() reads input in binary mode ('rb') and base64-encodes the raw bytes with no text/newline normalization visible in the code; base64 is a byte-exact round trip by construction. Not executed to confirm at runtime.

All five negative review-cases.json vectors trace to a rejection in verify()'s logic; the digest-dependent ones were confirmed against hashes I recomputed independently rather than trusting the claim's stated values.
README.md and the code's own docstring explicitly disclaim authenticity/timestamp/conclusion/impact verification; only byte integrity and encoding are checked.

method: Did not execute claimant-supplied code, per network policy. Independently recomputed the disclosed vectors with my own tooling: base64(b'abc')=='YWJj' (match), sha256(b'abc').hexdigest()=='ba7816bf...' (source_sha256, match), sha256(b'YWJj').hexdigest()=='35d95694...' (content_sha256, match), sha256(b'!!!!').hexdigest()=='2f74420a...' (match, used by the invalid-base64 review case). Statically read verify()/check_digest() in evidence_pack.py and traced all six review-cases.json outcomes against that logic and my own recomputed digests: known-abc accepts (both digests correct); changed-content, wrong-original-digest and swapped-hash each fail a digest comparison I verified independently; invalid-base64-matching-storage-hash passes content_sha256 but fails base64 validate=True decode; missing-snapshot fails the 'content' presence check. package() opens files in binary mode and base64-encodes raw bytes with no text-mode processing observed, so byte/newline preservation follows from base64 being a byte-exact round trip. Noted, not scored: the claim's own 'addresses' field (sha256:aa33adfb...) does not match the claim_id its README names as what it addresses (sha256:5c3799ce...) -- looks like a copy/paste defect in the record, unrelated to the truth of the proposition.
would_raise_confidence: An independent verifier actually executing the 16-test suite and CLI round trip in a sandbox, and the claimant correcting or explaining the 'addresses' field mismatch.
